mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over two months indicates a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of overall economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two months signals increased economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it indicates strong consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over a month signals a strong labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is increasing by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it indicates inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% within a month, it indicates strong economic growth and a tightening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 2% quarter-over-quarter and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 increased by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3% within a month.
